en.heading: National Heroes Day: remembering many lives, not one name
en.origin: The Philippine National Heroes Day honours people who contributed to the country's struggle for independence and to its civic history, rather than one named historical figure. Act No. 3827 established an official National Heroes Day in 1931 on the last Sunday of August. Later holiday legislation, including Republic Act No. 9492, placed the observance on the last Monday of August; the 2026 government calendar lists 31 August. The original law, later scheduling and the history being remembered are separate facts.

en.heading: 21 August: a national remembrance of Ninoy Aquino
en.origin: Ninoy Aquino Day recalls the assassination of former senator Benigno 'Ninoy' Aquino Jr. on 21 August 1983. The killing became a significant episode in the Philippines' path toward the restoration of democratic institutions. Republic Act No. 9256, approved on 25 February 2004, designated 21 August each year as a national special non-working holiday in his memory. The 2026 national proclamation lists it in that category. Although the date marks one person's death, this entry is a legally established national observance, not a personal anniversary merely indexed by a cultural calendar.
en.promoter: The Philippine Congress and the president established the national holiday through Republic Act No. 9256 in 2004.
en.purpose: Remember the 1983 assassination and reflect on civic participation, democratic freedoms and the political history of the Philippines.
